_note: The curated Claude Code picker: the fallback until Claude Code's own model list is discovered (runtime/cc_model_discovery.rs, ADR 0325), and the overlay that declares context windows. Once a probe succeeds the picker is exactly what Claude Code lists, so a row here is offered only before that. The reasoning_efforts list is still read for the effort vocabulary. include_str!() baked at compile time, parsed once via LazyLock. At most ONE entry may claim top capability: Fable is the tier above Opus, so an Opus entry must not be described as 'most capable', and only the NEWEST Fable row may claim it. Rows run newest version first, `default` at the head and the version-free aliases at the tail, which `the_model_rows_run_newest_version_first` enforces. An alias row (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) is labelled version-free on purpose: CC repoints those aliases over time. There is deliberately no `sonnet[1m]` / `claude-sonnet-5[1m]` row: `sonnet[1m]` has no effect once `sonnet` resolves to a Sonnet with a native 1M window. `claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]` is the one exception, kept so Sonnet 5.5 offers the same pair as Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. An optional `context_window` declares, in tokens, the window a session on that model actually runs under, read through `runtime::coding_agent_context_window`; absent means the models registry's answer stands. Set it only on a PINNED id, never on an alias row: `normalize_cc_model_id` folds old dated ids onto `sonnet`/`opus`/`haiku`. The `[1m]` rows leave it absent because the id-shape rule already answers 1M for them. An Opus point release such as `claude-opus-5-5` is its own pinned row, not a relabel of `claude-opus-5`.
